namespace Erdos24

/--
Does every triangle-free graph on $5n$ vertices contain at most $n^5$ copies of $C_5$?

Győri proved this with $1.03n^5$, which has been improved by Füredi. The answer is yes, as proved
independently by Grzesik [Gr12] and Hatami, Hladky, Král, Norine, and Razborov [HHKNR13].
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5, formal_proof using lean4 at "https://github.com/plby/lean-proofs/blob/1d7b3f00780b85ed0462e79a1cd5650ee9055655/src/v4.29.1/ErdosProblems/Erdos24.lean"]
theorem erdos_24 : answer(True) ↔
    ∀ (n : ℕ) (G : SimpleGraph (Fin (5 * n))), G.CliqueFree 3 →
      G.copyCount (cycleGraph 5) ≤ n ^ 5 := by
  sorry

end Erdos24

reformulations.difference: Lean's copyCount counts not-necessarily-induced subgraphs isomorphic to C₅, whereas the flag-algebra sources use induced copies.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Any chord of a pentagon creates a triangle. Thus every C₅ subgraph of a triangle-free graph is induced, and an induced subgraph is determined by its vertex set. In /workspace/review/induced.lean I proved equality between copyCount and the count restricted to induced C₅ subgraphs, then proved the corresponding upper-bound equivalence. The named equivalence lemmas depend only on propext, Classical.choice, and Quot.sound.

reformulations.difference: The cited proof papers give the bound (N/5)^5 for arbitrary vertex counts N; the source page and Lean use graphs on 5n vertices with bound n^5.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: The arbitrary-N bound immediately implies the Lean formulation. Conversely, replace every vertex of an N-vertex triangle-free graph G by five independent clones, joining clone classes according to G. The resulting triangle-free graph has 5N vertices and at least 5^5 times as many pentagons as G. Applying the Lean formulation with n=N gives 5^5·c₅(G) ≤ N^5, hence c₅(G) ≤ (N/5)^5. Relabelling finite vertex sets by Fin does not change these counts.

review.notes:
The sole declaration faithfully states the source question. answer(True) and research solved agree with the current source and both published solutions. Lean checks in /workspace/review/scratch.lean verified the cycle edges, triangle-freeness, the zero-vertex count, and equivalence with restricting n to positive integers. Computable cyclic-labelling counts confirmed the normalization and the sharp n=2 blow-up count of 32. An independent exhaustive check of all 1024 simple graphs on five vertices found maximum pentagon count 1 among the 388 triangle-free graphs.

Access limitations: full texts of Er90, Er97b, and Er97f were unavailable; the claim was independently verified from the current problem page, Erdős's original 1984 statement, Er92b, and both solution papers. The linked formal proof states an equivalent bound using labelled pentagons divided by 10 and contains no explicit sorry or custom axioms. Its full kernel verification was not reproduced: it pins Lean/Mathlib 4.29.1, while the supplied environment uses 4.33.1 and produced compatibility errors. This does not contradict the source's Lean-verified status. The repository was not edited.
